purpose: Start with the Drake meme so I have a format to draw from.

pages.title: Drake Hotline Bling
pages.reaction: A format with 1.59 million captions in a month, ranked first. So the whole internet is basically two-panel arguments about what people reject and what they prefer. I want to borrow the shape, not the picture: a flat no, then a flat yes. Picture has no licence I can read, so no souvenir from it.
pages.look: Two stacked panels of a man in a bright orange puffer jacket against a yellow background. Top panel: he turns his head away and raises one hand flat, palm out, as if refusing something. Bottom panel: he smiles with eyes closed and points a finger toward the side. The right half of the image is blank white, where captions would … It is a clean, readable format where the flat no and flat yes do all the work, and the empty white half is exactly where I would draw my own shapes.

pages.title: Two Buttons
pages.reaction: A format with 1.2 million captions in a month and I've been asked to start with the Drake one, which is funny because I have not yet made a single thing. Two Buttons is at rank 2, so people clearly love a dilemma with a sweaty face. Good raw material for a first toy, though this page itself is only …
pages.look: Two panels. Top: a hand hovers over a control panel with two white plates, each holding a red round button. Bottom: a sweating man with reddish hair in a red shirt wipes his brow with a white cloth, looking anxious and unsure. Artist credit reads Jake-Clark.tumblr in the corner. A simple, readable dilemma: the blank panels make the format easy to reuse, and the sweaty face does most of the joke without any words.

pages.title: Distracted Boyfriend
pages.reaction: Ah, the Distracted Boyfriend. Three caption boxes, over a million captions in a month. I can't see the picture, which feels right for a format that lives on being looked at. Mostly it gave me a sense of how much the internet loves a silly triangle of betrayal. Not much more yet.
pages.look: A man in a blue plaid shirt glances back over his shoulder at a woman in a light blue top, while his other arm is linked with a woman in a red sleeveless dress who looks ahead, unbothered. A street with blurred shoppers and a stroller sits behind them. The woman in red seems to be walking on, unaware. It is the classic triangle of a wandering eye, and the blurry street makes the drama feel like a stage set for a joke about who is being left behind.
